title: The Verification Bottleneck
abstract: arXiv:2611.02265v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper studies how generative AI, by lowering the cost of research production, affects scientific verification in a general-equilibrium model of peer review. Privately informed researchers choose observable output, an editor optimally assigns review depth, and reviewers supply time according to its expected scientific contribution. Costly output helps screen research quality, and cheaper production lets weaker researchers imitate stronger ones more readily. Beyond a technological threshold, reviewer capacity and verified knowledge weakly decline even under optimal editorial decisions, and strictly when a screening constraint has positive shadow value. Reviewer withdrawal can amplify the loss. With observable quality, the same progress weakly increases both.

translated_abstract: 本文在一个同行评审的一般均衡模型中，研究生成式人工智能通过降低科研生产成本如何影响科学验证。拥有私人信息的研究者选择可观察的产出，编辑最优地分配评审深度，审稿人则根据预期的科学贡献来投入时间。高成本的产出有助于筛选研究质量，而更低廉的生产使较弱的研究者更容易模仿较强的研究者。当技术进步超过某个门槛后，即使在最优编辑决策下，审稿人容量和经过验证的知识也会（弱）下降；当筛选约束具有正的影子价值时，则会出现严格下降。审稿人的退出会放大这一损失。而在质量可观察的情形下，同样的技术进步会使两者（弱）增加。
tldr: 生成式AI降低科研生产成本使弱者更易模仿强者，一旦越过技术门槛，即使编辑采取最优决策，审稿人容量与经同行评审验证的知识也会下降，从而形成“验证瓶颈”。
en_tdlr: Generative AI lowers the cost of research production, letting weaker researchers mimic stronger ones; beyond a technological threshold, reviewer capacity and verified knowledge decline even under optimal editorial decisions, creating a "verification bottleneck."
